clue.text: Tending to justify very little — typical!

parts.note: the word very made small, that is shortened to its abbreviation V
something typical of a thing is indicative of it

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a small justification is just what you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very little' reads as a phrase meaning hardly any; it is 'very' cut down to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A vindicative argument serves to clear or uphold someone, so it tends to justify them.

clue.text: Saint thoughtless about fast days gets obese finally

indicators.note: the word for thoughtless goes round the word for fast days

parts.note: vain in its sense of empty-headed or foolish
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of the word obese

explanation.surface: A careless saint who ignores the fasting season ends up fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Valentine is the martyr whose feast day is 14 February.

clue.text: Opening number's warble cut short

parts.note: No is the abbreviation for number, and the 's is added to it

indicators.note: the word for warble loses its final letter

parts.note: to warble is to trill like a bird

explanation.surface: A song's opening number has its warbling clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Each nostril is an opening of the nose.

clue.text: Reducing the effectiveness of mischief-maker with exposure

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil or child
giving something an airing exposes it to view or to the air

explanation.surface: A troublemaker's revelations undermine something's effectiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or damage it, so it works less well.

clue.text: A pine at full length

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A pine tree stretched out to its full height.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying along something means stretched out over its whole length.

clue.text: Incorporate tricky clue in last bit of crossword

indicators.note: something tricky is twisted and devious, so these letters are rearranged
takes the final letter of the word crossword

explanation.surface: A setter slips a devious clue into the final corner of the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' shuffles CLUE and IN together with D, the end of 'crossword'.
explanation.definitionFit: To include is to take something in as part of a whole, a synonym of incorporate.

clue.text: Woman in charge in a particular period

indicators.note: the abbreviation for in charge sits inside the word for a period

parts.note: an era is a particular period of history
IC is the initials of in charge, as on a military duty roster (officer i/c)

explanation.surface: A woman takes command during a certain era.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Rhythms still changing

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of still are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Musical rhythms are still in a state of flux.
explanation.definitionFit: A lilt is a light, swinging rhythm in speech or music.

clue.text: Plant engagement ring on this?

definitions.meaning: a name for okra, and also for kidney vetch
a woman's ring finger, where an engagement ring is worn

explanation.surface: Would you put an engagement ring on a plant?
explanation.definitionFit: Lady's finger is a common name for okra and kidney vetch, and literally a woman's finger, where an engagement ring goes.

clue.text: Denounce professional writer

parts.note: pro is the short form of professional
a scribe is one who writes, historically a copyist

explanation.surface: A professional writer is told to condemn something.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to condemn or forbid something formally.

clue.text: Almanacs record the man accompanying me on journeys

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
he is the pronoun for a man
rides are journeys on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone's travel log records the man who goes with them on trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemerides are tables giving the daily positions of heavenly bodies, a kind of astronomical almanac.

clue.text: You'd get at least 20 asses for this Roman money!

definitions.text: You'd get at least 20 asses for this Roman money!

parts.words: You'd get at least 20 asses for this Roman money!
parts.note: the as was a small Roman coin, and one silver Roman coin was worth ten of them, so two or more such coins buy at least twenty

explanation.surface: A joke about trading money for a herd of donkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'asses' looks like donkeys, but it is the plural of the as, a Roman copper coin; the plural answer means at least two coins worth ten each.
explanation.definitionFit: Denarii, plural of denarius, were silver coins of ancient Rome, originally worth ten asses.

clue.text: Food — something sickly, we hear, and something whipped

indicators.note: tells us we take the sound of the word, spelt differently

parts.note: goo is sickly-sweet sticky stuff, and is said aloud here
a lash is a stroke of the whip

explanation.surface: A dish described as something nauseating plus a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian stew of meat and paprika.

clue.text: Hogwash from second bard

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare, whose first name was William, Will for short

explanation.surface: Nonsense coming from a minor poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hogwash' reads as nonsense, but is meant literally: swill is the slop fed to pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash originally meant kitchen slops given to pigs, the same as pig swill.

clue.text: Active in business but crawling maybe?

definitions.meaning: involved in and up to date with current affairs or activity
the crawl is a swimming stroke, so a crawler is in the water swimming

explanation.surface: Someone busy at work, though perhaps creeping about.
explanation.definitionFit: In the swim is an idiom for being involved in what is going on, and literally describes someone swimming the front crawl.

clue.text: The man's surrounded by stars in wordy book

indicators.note: the contraction for the man is goes inside the constellation's name

parts.note: Taurus is a constellation, a group of stars
the man is becomes he's

explanation.surface: A man is ringed by celebrities in a book full of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing words with similar meanings.

clue.text: This tower to a new design is most noble

indicators.note: rebuilding to a new design means the letters of this tower are rearranged

explanation.surface: An architect claims a redesigned tower is the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: The worthiest person is the most deserving and honourable.

clue.text: I will get loud with ego out of control — English fanatic?

indicators.note: letters running wild are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A loud, egotistical Englishman is labelled a zealot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I will' at the start is not I'LL: 'I' supplies its letter and 'will get' is only a link, as is 'with' between the two anagram words.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideologue is a dogmatic follower of an ideology, arguably a kind of zealot, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A gee-gee restricted by fat — one falling behind

indicators.note: the pieces are held in by the word for fat around them

parts.note: lard is pig fat
a children's word for a horse, abbreviated GG

explanation.surface: An overweight racehorse trails behind the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is someone who lags or straggles behind.

clue.text: Person tending another — energy-draining occupation

indicators.note: removing the energy, as if drained from it

parts.note: a career is one's working occupation
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A tiring job looking after someone saps your strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after someone sick, old or disabled.

clue.text: With use of lifting gear managed to get in crate

indicators.note: the word for managed is put inside the word for crate

parts.note: a cage is a crate-like enclosure
to run a business is to manage it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: Someone squeezes into a crate using a hoist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranage is the use of a crane, or the charge made for it.

clue.text: As a woman, I rage and go bananas

indicators.note: slang for crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman is driven to fury and madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' is part of the fodder, not of the indicator; 'bananas' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Shell that's yellow floating on French sea

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second, as if floating on it

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A yellow shell bobs on the waves of a French sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An ormer is an edible sea snail, the abalone, with an ear-shaped shell.

clue.text: Local dignitary — man disappearing in tree

indicators.note: the word man vanishes from the longer word

parts.note: an alderman is a senior member of a local council
taken as written

explanation.surface: A councillor vanishes into a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family growing near water.

clue.text: A graduate with modest accommodation is embarrassed

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
a shed is a simple, humble building

explanation.surface: A graduate living in a humble shack is ashamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means made to feel embarrassed or ashamed.

clue.text: Artist married wicked robber

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is a crossword artist

indicators.note: something wicked is twisted, so the letters of married are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter married a villainous thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram raider is a thief who smashes a vehicle into a shop front to steal goods.

clue.text: Affirms the bible, but with words of hesitation

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible
er is a sound of hesitation, here in the plural

explanation.surface: Someone swears on the Bible, but with stammering doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly or assert, so avers means affirms.

clue.text: A symbol of hope in countries where they don't get cross

definitions.text: A symbol of hope in countries where they don't get cross

parts.words: A symbol of hope in countries where they don't get cross
parts.note: the humanitarian emblem used in Muslim countries instead of the cross; 'get cross' reads as getting angry

explanation.surface: Some nations are so calm they never lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get cross' looks like getting angry, but means using the Red Cross emblem; Muslim nations use a different symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Crescent is the emblem of the relief movement in Islamic countries, replacing the Red Cross.
